custom:view_worth.//: A grid, not absolute positions. Absolute `nodes` are documented as authoritative under layoutMode 'custom' and are silently ignored by `stemma render` for a view whose members come from ElementIds — verified on a two-box workspace, so this is the tool's gap rather than this file's. The constraint is honoured, so the composition is stated as one.
custom:view_worth.//grid: Rows are as tall as their tallest member, so a multi-line box in column 1 stretches the gap between the teams beside it. Both services therefore sit in row 0 — one tall row, then three tight ones — instead of one in row 0 and one in row 1, which stretched two gaps and made the stack look ragged.
custom:view_worth.//offsets: Row 0 puts the correct service level with the lump. It belongs below and apart — the emptiness around it is the argument — so it is nudged down. An offset rides on top of the solved arrangement instead of replacing it, which is the whole reason to prefer a constraint over coordinates.
custom:view_worth.//edges: Default docking is left/right, which routed every arrow out of a team's left side and all the way around the canvas. Leaving right and arriving left is the only reading that matches the sentence.
custom:view_worth.//shapes: Ink, not model: it asserts nothing about a system, so it must never become an element. Only one label survives — a second reading 'four teams integrated' said what four visible arrows already say, and it landed on top of the lump's text.
